newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, spreads still strong.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, spreads still strong.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer, the market regaining some of its poise after dipping ahead of a much-talked of sharp hike in LME stocks on Friday, traders said.
LME stocks rose 26,100 tonnes to 191,750 tonnes.

Expectations of a sharp increase in LME stocks, following a prolonged period of strong backwardation in London and an LME cash premium over spot COMEX, caused some of the selling earlier in the week, Smith Barney's David Rinehimer said.
The LME backwardation also eased during the week from a high of some $345 to briefly below $195, to strengthen once again Friday to $230/$240 by COMEX close Friday.
Talk of a stock hike and the LME saying it was monitoring the copper spreads contributed to an easing of the backwardation, traders said.
Most active March COMEX settled 2.55 cents firmer at 103.75 cents per pound, traded 103.90 to 100.50 cents.
Volume was estimated at 15,000 lots compared to Thursday's 11,255 lots.

"There appears to be less concern about a supply squeeze over the next two-to-four weeks," Rinehimer said. "But you are still looking at a relatively tight inventory situation relative to usage, right during a period when demand is seasonally the strongest."
March traded in a wide range this week with a high of 107.65 cents and a low of 100.40 cents, ending the week 2.90 cents weaker.

"We are not going to shift to a surplus until the second half of the year. Downside should not be too much under a dollar, and upside could be above the recent highs, particularly if we get more demand from China," Rinehimer said.
